posts.text:
This map gets shared as 'what Taiwan officially claims' — all of mainland China, Mongolia, even a slice of Russia. Part of that hasn't been true since 2002.

a thread 🧭🗺️

1/ The claim to the mainland is real and still on the books. The Republic of China's 1947 constitution was written for a government that then ruled mainland China, and it was never rewritten when that government retreated to Taiwan in 1949.

2/ Since the early 1990s Taiwan hasn't acted on that claim. Constitutional changes under President Lee Teng-hui in 1991-92 accepted, in practice, that the Chinese Communist Party governs the mainland — no invasion is coming from Taipei.

3/ Mongolia is the outdated part of the map. Taiwan's constitution briefly counted Mongolia as lost territory too, but in October 2002 Taiwan formally recognised Mongolian independence and dropped it from official maps.

4/ The sliver of Russia usually shown is Tuva, once Tannu Uriankhai, on Mongolia's northern border. Taiwan never separately renounced a claim there, but a 2012 government statement said Outer Mongolia was never part of its territory — and Tuva rides on that same claim.

5/ So the accurate version of this map is smaller than the viral one: mainland China, yes, still constitutionally. Mongolia and Tuva, no — quietly dropped over the last two decades, even though the old maximal maps keep circulating.

6/ None of this is likely to change soon — amending Taiwan's constitution needs a legislative supermajority and a public referendum, and Beijing has said redrawing the map would itself be treated as a step toward independence.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
